audit.why: The spike timings hold: Urgot at 3-5 with Q zoning the dash, at 6 with the execute, and at first item where Yasuo's low base resists melt. Yasuo has no stage that beats a Juggernaut here.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page states three times — spikes[1].text, content.mid and whys[4] — that Urgot's R 'ignores his Wind Wall entirely because it's a suppression, not a projectile'. That is backwards. Urgot's R is flagged projectile, 'can be blocked by Wind Wall-class effects', and so are his Q and his E. Yasuo's own W is flagged blocksProjectiles: 'deletes enemy projectile damage entirely'. The page also never mentions Way of the Wanderer's shield.
audit.why: This is the single most dangerous claim in the matchup: it tells the player to throw a 100-second ultimate into a wall that deletes it. It is the same class of error as the Azir/Yasuo case in the calibration list. Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17s for 4 seconds, so baiting it out leaves a 21-second window at rank 1 where all three of Urgot's projectiles land freely.
audit.corrected: All three Wind Wall claims rewritten to say the wall blocks Q, E and R, with the bait-then-commit sequencing and the 25s/4s numbers. dontsFull[0].d now names the passive shield as the thing to force out first, and dosFull[2].d carries the 21-second free window.
sources: ownerKit Q, E, R (all flagged projectile, blockable by Wind Wall)

edits.before: Level 6 R flips and executes through Wind Wall, making your all-in far stronger than his.
edits.after: Level 6 R is a chem-drill projectile — Wind Wall eats it, so bait the wall first.

edits.before: R Fear Beyond Death is death on a target this squishy: once you W him below the flip threshold, the flip-and-execute ignores his Wind Wall entirely because it's a suppression, not a projectile. Don't waste R early — hold it to punish any greedy EQ trade or his all-in.
edits.after: R Fear Beyond Death is death on a target this squishy, but it is a projectile and Wind Wall deletes it — 4 seconds of wall on a 25s cooldown. Force the wall out with a Q first, then flip and execute inside those 21 seconds. Never open a trade with R.

edits.before: From 3 onward you dictate — bait his E off a minion, Q the landing spot, W him down while he's dashless. At 6 your R flips and executes through Wind Wall since suppression ignores projectiles, so any greedy trade dies.
edits.after: From 3 onward you dictate — bait his E off a minion, Q the landing spot, W him down while he's dashless. At 6 remember Wind Wall blocks your Q, E and R alike, so make him spend it before you commit anything.

edits.after: Your Q Corrosive Charge outranges everything Yasuo has bar an E-dash onto you, but Wind Wall eats the shell, so throw it where he must walk rather than at him. Bait his E off a minion, then Q the ground he lands on and W Purge him down while he has no dash to escape.

notes: The 'R ignores Wind Wall because it's a suppression' claim was live on the page in three places and is flatly contradicted by both kits — Urgot's R carries the projectile flag and Yasuo's W deletes enemy projectiles. This was the highest-value correction in my slice. What I could NOT verify and did not assert: whether Wind Wall blocks the Q shell's ground explosion as well as the initial cast, and whether Urgot's E charge is stopped by the wall or merely has its projectile component blocked — the kit only tells me the E is flagged blockable, so I wrote 'blocks your Q, E and R alike' without detailing the mechanism.
